scope: Corollary 5.5 (Conditional density domination) of the manuscript “Quantum Depletion and Momentum Distribution in the Dilute Hard-Sphere Bose Gas” (preprints/Quantum-Depletion-and-Momentum-Distribution-in-the-Dilute-Hard-Sphere-Bose-Gas-October-5-2026/Quantum-Depletion-in-the-Dilute-Hard-Sphere-Bose-Gas.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 267 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9e8a9907a3ac0811), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 40. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix good data and a set of route labels S ⊂ I with a bounded number of labels per site. In a product of their free bridge probabilities, condition on individual cutoffs and any selection of avoidance checks, including checks against fixed outside paths. The paths with labels in I \ S need only satisfy their individual cutoffs; the frozen paths remain those of the fixed good data. Every specified q labels have joint marginal density at most Cq relative to the product of their Bi. The conclusion also holds conditional on the values of all other labels. A uniform-midpoint insertion has the additional density expense CDCx for each inserted marginal, or in an augmented integral retaining the common midpoint, and replacing one free midpoint density by that of a neighboring label has expense (5.17).
